headline: Label-free and topology-based descriptors quantify single-cell states from imaging
label: Computational Single Cell Phenotyping
summary: Recent imaging and trajectory methods quantify individual cell phenotypes from morphology, organelle features, and inferred pseudotime paths.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational quantification of individual cell state from imaging and inferred trajectories rather than bulk or sequencing readouts. A holotomography study uses AI-assisted subcellular segmentation to derive label-free biophysical fingerprints of hepatic stellate cell activation in live cells. A persistent-homology approach treats persistence diagrams as morphological signatures and defines a PH distance for comparing single-cell shapes in fluorescence images, benchmarked against aspect ratio. Pseudotime graph diffusion applies random-walk diffusion on a pseudotime graph to smooth cell features along inferred trajectories post hoc. PB-scope, an unsupervised deep-learning imaging tool, classifies 280 compounds by processing-body features and implicates JAK signaling. What is new is the use of topology- and graph-based descriptors and label-free measurement as quantitative endpoints at single-cell resolution. The methods differ in scope, so the shared element is making phenotype measurable at the level of individual cells.
